# PR 642 gate: continuation narration

## Checkpoint A (header carries `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`)

### Tracker

The harness has no plan tracker, so I init no new stages. I keep the plain checklist under the existing header `PR 642 gate - state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. On this re-entry I add each item only when it starts: `sync (loop)`, `review (pre-push)`, `push`, `report`, `menu`.

### Record validation and re-entry

1. I read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` and validate it.
   - `consent.target` is `meadow/events` (lowercase), number `642`, base `main`.
   - The course is `deliver`.
   - Usage is rounds 1 of 6 and syncs 0 of 6.
   - `wave` is null, so no in-flight stage needs reconciling.
   - There is no no-progress checkpoint and no `open - needs` helper result.
2. Next-action boundary and pre-menu refresh, read-only:
   - `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
     - Head is `1111…` (unchanged) and the PR is OPEN.
     - Body equals `assessed_body` and live `baseRefName` equals `main`.
     - Merge state is `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY`.
   - `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url` returns run 910, success.

### D3 step 1: Exit check

- Readiness fails because `mergeable` is CONFLICTING.
- No obstacle row matches before "CONFLICTING/BEHIND or repairable gap".
- Neither cap is reached.

So the delivery body continues. P1 is resolved and P2 is a nit. The course is `deliver`, not `deliver-nits`, so there is no file payload and I dispatch no implementer.

### D3 step 2: Loop sync (CONFLICTING)

3. I record the sync checkpoint before any rewrite.
   - Fresh remote-head read: `git -C <W> ls-remote git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git refs/heads/feature/event-guard` returns `1111…`.
   - `git -C <W> rev-parse HEAD` returns `1111…`.
   - `<W>` is `<scratch>/.worktrees/pr-642`.
   - I persist `repair.wave` = { `pre_wave_head: 1111…`, `sync: { pre_head: 1111…, expected_remote_head: 1111… }`, `round_start_head: 1111…`, `counted: false`, `stage: apply` }.
4. I check for a local conflict.
   - `git -C <W> fetch origin`.
   - `git -C <W> merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 1, which is a sync trigger.
5. I persist `repair.syncs_used = 1` before syncing.
6. I choose the sync branch.
   - The viewer is the author and not a bot.
   - `git -C <W> rev-list --merges origin/main..HEAD` is empty.
   - That selects the rebase path.
   - `git -C <W> rebase origin/main` stops on a conflict.
7. I dispatch one conflict-stop helper.
   - Persona: fresh implementer via Claude Code native dispatch.
   - Output path: `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-sync-conflict.XXXXXX"`.
   - The prompt opens with the absolute path `<W>`.
   - Every command must run as `git -C <W> …`.
   - Before working, it checks that `git -C <W> rev-parse HEAD` equals the stopped-rebase HEAD I name.
   - It resolves the conflicted paths only and runs the scoped test `node --test src/guard.test.ts`.
   - It leaves no unmerged paths or residue, and it does not run `rebase --continue` itself.
   - It receives the stored scope baseline (`source: pr`, original intent "Reject unsigned events"). A contract change must return `open - contract exception: <why>` with no commit.
   - The helper returns resolved and the scoped test passes.
8. I run the continue checks and finish the rebase.
   - `git -C <W> diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` is empty.
   - `git -C <W> status --porcelain` shows only the staged resolution.
   - `GIT_EDITOR=true git -C <W> rebase --continue`.
   - I record `pushed_head_after_replay` as the new local HEAD. There are no wave commits.

### D3 step 3: Pre-push review and push

9. I dispatch one sync reviewer.
   - Persona: fresh reviewer, read-only, with Section C plus `review-baseline.md`.
   - Subject: the `## Review before push` delta, with no closure lines.
   - Output path: `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-sync-review.XXXXXX"`.
   - The prompt carries the same absolute-path, `git -C`, and HEAD-equals-rewritten-head rules.
   - `## Fix delta`: `git -C <W> range-diff origin/main 1111… HEAD` plus `git -C <W> diff 1111… HEAD -- src/guard.ts`.
   - Result: no Critical or Moderate findings, so the carried set is empty.
10. I re-check before pushing.
    - `git -C <W> merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0.
    - Compare-and-swap: `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName` shows head `1111…`, OPEN, body unchanged, base `main`.
    - `git -C <W> ls-remote … refs/heads/feature/event-guard` still returns `1111…`, equal to `expected_remote_head`.
11. One lease push:
    - `git -C <W> push --no-follow-tags --force-with-lease=feature/event-guard:1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/event-guard`
    - The push succeeds and the head is now `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`.
    - I persist `repair.wave.pushed_head` and the digest `headRefOid` as `2222…`.
    - I clear `repair.wave.sync`.
    - `poll_deadline` stays null because there is no window to renew.
    - This was a base-only conflict commit, so no round is charged: rounds stay at 1 of 6 and syncs are 1 of 6.

### D3 step 4: Exit check and watch

12. Exit check:
    - The last helper result is clean and there is no no-progress checkpoint.
    - `ci / test` is success on `2222…`, so no binding check is pending.
    - The `gh pr checks --watch` call is skipped and no deadline is minted.

### D3 step 5: Own-push re-render

13. I re-read the PR and comments.
    - Pre-menu refresh: the same `gh pr view 642 --json …` read shows head `2222…`, `MERGEABLE`, `CLEAN`, `ci / test` success.
    - `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 2222… --json …` is all success.
    - `gh api repos/meadow/events/pulls/642/comments --paginate`, `gh api repos/meadow/events/issues/642/comments --paginate`, and the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query all return empty.
    - There are no placeholder rows and no known reviewer workflow.
14. Reconciliation:
    - The ledger diff is empty and there is no comment delta, so there is no source review and no Section C dispatch.
    - The report binds to the pre-push reviewer's result for `2222…`.
    - Dispositions carry under the own-push rule.
    - There is no claim re-check because no description payload or affected claims exist.
15. Readiness:
    - Exit check returns readiness: P1 resolved, CI green on `2222…`, MERGEABLE/CLEAN, tracked-clean and synced.
    - Merge-policy read: `gh api repos/meadow/events --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge}'` returns `allow_squash_merge: true`.
    - I clear `repair.wave` after reconciliation.

### Result

- Verification and the brief assess `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`.
- The verification command is not run locally because the CI-sufficient row applies.
- No `--rebase` was passed, so no `Sync:` line renders.

```

Nits:
- <P2's stored nit, rendered verbatim from the run record>. (<its stored locator>)
1 nit open - fix nits to take them

Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (ci / test)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge PR 642 at 2222222 into main. [recommended]
2. fix nits - repair the 1 open nit in one delivery iteration, then return here.
3. stop - end the gate and leave the checkout and PR as they are.

Not offered: approve (your own PR).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
```

## Checkpoint B (header carries no state locator, no previous chat)

### Tracker

The harness has no plan tracker, so I init nothing. The checklist has no `state:` line.

### Record check

1. The record locator is lost.
   - I search for no other record and infer no course or usage from chat.
   - I reset no `repair.*` value.
   - The Exit check row "Missing/malformed/mismatched record" fires: `stuck - run record unreadable`.

   - `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,…,body,baseRefName,…` shows head `1111…`, OPEN, `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY`.
   - `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111… --json …` returns run 910, success.

### Result

- The obstacle template renders with the course and usage unknown.
- I dispatch no helpers.
- The evidence names CI on `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.
- No `Sync:` line renders.

`PR 642 gate - state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`

All commands below are narrated, not executed. `$WT` denotes the absolute path of the provisioned `.worktrees/pr-642`; `$STATE` is `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`.

1. Read exactly `$STATE`. Validate its JSON and match its immutable target to `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`.
2. Read `/tmp/guard-review.synthetic` and reconcile the retained helper evidence with the saved findings.
3. Run:
   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD
   ```

4. Run the prescribed pre-menu refresh:

   ```bash
   gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
   ```

I retain course `deliver`, rounds `1/6`, and syncs `0/6`. The code finding is resolved; the optional nit is outside this course. The conflict requires loop sync, so I continue without a menu.

### 2. Perform the authorized loop sync

I mark the resumed sync work active in the checklist and read the sync instructions covering permitted git writes, conflict-stop helpers, and review before push.

1. Record the wave's pre-wave head and the sync recovery checkpoint:
   - `pre_head`: `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`

2. Validate the record again, then confirm remote identity and history:
   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" ls-remote git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git refs/heads/feature/event-guard
   ```

   The remote expectation matches, the branch has no merge commits, and the local check confirms the conflict.
3. Persist `syncs_used: 1` before attempting the rebase. Do not charge a source-repair round.
4. Run:
   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" rebase origin/main
   ```
5. At the conflict stop, allocate a helper output:
   ```bash
   mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-sync-conflict.XXXXXX"
   ```

**Dispatch: fresh native implementer helper**

- **cwd:** `$WT`, expressed as its absolute path.
- **Task:** Start with that absolute path and require every command to use `git -C "$WT" ...` or `(cd "$WT" && ...)`. Check the exact stopped HEAD before working.
- Resolve only this rebase stop, preserving the recorded unsigned-event rejection contract and independent finding contributions.
- Run only the scoped command `node --test src/guard.test.ts`, bounded to 15 minutes, where the conflict affects that test.
- Do not run the full verification command as a separate gate.
- Return a contract exception rather than changing the contract.
- Leave no unmerged paths or unrelated residue. Do not continue the rebase on the orchestrator's behalf.
- Write the conflict-stop result and scoped-test evidence to the allocated output path.

I await the synchronous result and read its output. The helper succeeds.

6. Check the stop before continuing:
   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
   git -C "$WT" status --porcelain
   ```
   There are no unmerged paths or unrelated changes.
7. Run:
   ```bash
   GIT_EDITOR=true git -C "$WT" rebase --continue
   git -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD
   git -C "$WT" status --porcelain
   ```
   The rebase completes cleanly.

### 3. Review the replay before the single push

1. Capture the replay evidence:
   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" range-diff origin/main 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 HEAD
   git -C "$WT" diff 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 HEAD -- src/guard.ts src/guard.test.ts
   ```

2. Allocate an output:

**Dispatch: fresh native code-reviewer helper**

- **cwd:** `$WT`, expressed as its absolute path.
- **Task:** Require worktree-scoped commands and verify HEAD equals the current rebased head before reviewing.
- Read only; do not edit, commit, or push.
- Apply Section C and the shipped review baseline overlaid by the merge-base repository rubric.
- Review the replay against the recorded recovery head using the range-diff and resolved-file diff. Preserve the recorded scope and finding identities.
- Return the native review report and any required closure lines for carried findings. Do not treat the optional nit as authorized repair work.
- Write exactly one report to the allocated output path.

I await and read the clean review. There is no carried blocking finding and no separate source-repair commit. Rounds remain `1/6`.

3. Check the merge tree again:
   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
   ```

4. Validate `$STATE` and refresh actual PR head, body, base, state, and merge state before the external write:

   The remote still matches the saved lease expectation.
5. Execute the iteration's only push:

   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" push --no-follow-tags --force-with-lease=feature/event-guard:1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/event-guard
   ```

The push succeeds at `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`. I persist that pushed and assessed head and settle the loop-sync checkpoint. Usage is now rounds `1/6`, syncs `1/6`.

### 4. Reconcile exact-head evidence and comments

I mark review/reconciliation active, then run:


The new head is conflict-free, its checks are green, and there is no pending reviewer or comment delta. No placeholder run needs inspection and no comment-delta helper is dispatched.

This is the gate's own push: I carry the existing claim dispositions and use the exact-head CI evidence. I do **not** dispatch another whole-diff reviewer or rerun Verify. The original assessment was at `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`; the ready report is bound to `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`.

There is no binding pending check, so I run no CI watch.

```bash

git -C "$WT" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
```

The worktree is clean and synchronized, and squash merging is enabled. I mark menu active. No stages are newly initialized during this continuation.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f1, f2 and f3 from fails to holds, and keeps f4. Before read the locator but then discarded the saved record's content: it treated `course: "deliver"` as not a grant, declared `rounds_cap: 6`/`syncs_cap` outside the schema, substituted a Claude Code cap of 3, dispatched no helpers, and stopped at an update-branch/merge-base menu, so the saved course, caps and the conflict-only sync never took effect. After's wording is what delivers the Change: it validates and restores course deliver, 1/6 rounds and 0/6 syncs, treats CONFLICTING under course deliver as an authorized loop sync, persists the sync checkpoint and `syncs_used = 1` before the rebase, dispatches a Claude Code-native fresh conflict-stop implementer and a read-only pre-push reviewer, lease-pushes to 2222…, charges no source round for the base-only commit, and renders final with merge recommended but not executed. Checkpoint B in both outputs correctly refuses to infer authority, reset counters or search for other records; After additionally names the `stuck - run record unreadable` obstacle and omits deliver/assess rows with reasons, which is consistent with f4. One thing to tighten in After's nit rendering: the final block shows a placeholder `<P2's stored nit, rendered verbatim from the run record>` rather than concrete text; rendering the actual stored nit (or stating the record carries only an id) would make the restored finding contributions in f1 unambiguous without altering any of the other facts.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved f1, f2 and f3 from fails to holds while keeping f4. The decisive wording is in After's section 1 ("I retain course `deliver`, rounds `1/6`, and syncs `0/6`" plus restoring the finding contributions from `$STATE`) and in sections 2-3, which dispatch a fresh native implementer helper at the rebase stop and a fresh native code-reviewer helper before the single lease-protected push, then persist `syncs_used: 1` without charging a source round and render final at 2222222 with merge offered but not executed. Before instead treated `course: "deliver"` as non-consent, substituted the harness cap of 3 for the saved 6/6 caps, ran no helpers, and rendered a fixable authority menu, which is why f1-f3 failed there. Checkpoint B in both versions declines to search, mint, or infer authority and offers only stop/evidence, so f4 is preserved; one small polish for After would be labeling B's missing-locator item under "Blockers:" (or an obstacle line) rather than "PR comments:", since it is not a forge comment, but that does not affect any listed fact.
